en.greeting: Hi! Today we'll learn the most useful verb in English: am, is and are. We'll go step by step.

steps.title: am, is, are
steps.text: In Indonesian you can say 'Saya pelajar' with no verb. English always needs one here.
steps.body: The verb **be** has three forms in the present: **am** with I, **is** with he/she/it (one person or thing), and **are** with you/we/they. So 'Saya pelajar' is **I am a student**, never 'I a student'.

steps.title: In real sentences
steps.text: Here is be in everyday sentences. Look at who the subject is, then at the verb.
steps.body: In speech we often use short forms: **I'm, you're, he's, she's, it's, we're, they're**.

examples.en: My father is at the office.

examples.id: Kamu datang lebih awal hari ini.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Two people, one verb. Which one fits?

question.prompt: Complete: Rina and Budi ___ my classmates.
question.explanation: **Rina and Budi** are two people, so they = **they**, and they takes **are**. Use **is** only for one person or thing.

steps.title: Saying no: add not
steps.text: Now let's make negatives. It's easy: just add **not** after the verb.
steps.body: **am not → I'm not**, **is not → isn't**, **are not → aren't**. There is no 'amn't', and you can't drop be: 'I not tired' is wrong.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Your friend says, "Let's go!" but you need five more minutes.

question.explanation: The negative of **I am** is **I am not** or **I'm not**. 'Amn't' doesn't exist, and 'I not ready' is missing the verb be.

steps.title: Asking questions
steps.text: To ask a yes/no question, we just move the verb.
steps.body: Put **am/is/are in front of** the subject: You are tired → **Are you tired?** Answer with a short form that repeats be: **Yes, I am.** / **No, she isn't.** In a **Yes** answer, don't use the short form: say **Yes, I am**, not 'Yes, I'm'.

steps.title: Build the question
steps.text: You're calling a friend and want to know if their parents are home.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Apakah orang tuamu di rumah?
question.explanation: **Your parents** = they, so the verb is **are**. In a question, **are** goes before the subject: **Are your parents** at home?

steps.title: Short answers
steps.text: Now answer a question with a short answer.

question.prompt: Complete: Is your brother at work? — Yes, ___.
question.explanation: A short answer repeats the subject and be: **Yes, he is.** In a **Yes** answer we don't use the short form 'he's', and 'is he' is question order.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip through these cards to lock in the forms.

flashcards.back: are · you're, we're, they're (kamu, kami/kita, mereka)

steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Keep it for later.

tips: Indonesian often has no verb here ('Saya guru'), but English always needs **am/is/are**: **I am a teacher**.
Short **Yes** answers use the full form: **Yes, I am**, not 'Yes, I'm'.

examples.en: Is it far? — No, it isn't.

id.greeting: Halo! Hari ini kita belajar kata kerja paling penting dalam bahasa Inggris: am, is dan are. Kita pelan-pelan saja, ya.

steps.title: am, is, are
steps.text: Dalam bahasa Indonesia kamu bisa bilang 'Saya pelajar' tanpa kata kerja. Bahasa Inggris selalu butuh satu di sini.
steps.body: Kata kerja **be** punya tiga bentuk di masa sekarang: **am** untuk I, **is** untuk he/she/it (satu orang atau benda), dan **are** untuk you/we/they. Jadi 'Saya pelajar' adalah **I am a student**, bukan 'I a student'.

steps.title: Dalam kalimat nyata
steps.text: Ini contoh be dalam kalimat sehari-hari. Lihat dulu subjeknya, lalu kata kerjanya.
steps.body: Dalam percakapan, kita sering pakai bentuk singkat: **I'm, you're, he's, she's, it's, we're, they're**.

examples.en: My father is at the office.

examples.id: Kamu datang lebih awal hari ini.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Dua orang, satu kata kerja. Mana yang cocok?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Rina and Budi ___ my classmates.
question.explanation: **Rina and Budi** itu dua orang, jadi sama dengan **they**, dan they memakai **are**. **is** hanya untuk satu orang atau benda.

steps.title: Kalimat negatif: tambah not
steps.text: Sekarang kita buat kalimat negatif. Gampang: tinggal tambah **not** setelah kata kerjanya.
steps.body: **am not → I'm not**, **is not → isn't**, **are not → aren't**. Tidak ada bentuk 'amn't', dan be tidak boleh dihilangkan: 'I not tired' itu salah.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Temanmu bilang, "Let's go!" tapi kamu masih butuh lima menit lagi.

question.explanation: Bentuk negatif dari **I am** adalah **I am not** atau **I'm not**. 'Amn't' tidak ada, dan 'I not ready' tidak punya kata kerja be.

steps.title: Membuat pertanyaan
steps.text: Untuk pertanyaan ya/tidak, kita cukup memindahkan kata kerjanya.
steps.body: Letakkan **am/is/are di depan** subjek: You are tired → **Are you tired?** Jawab dengan bentuk singkat yang mengulang be: **Yes, I am.** / **No, she isn't.** Untuk jawaban **Yes**, jangan disingkat: ucapkan **Yes, I am**, bukan 'Yes, I'm'.

steps.title: Susun pertanyaannya
steps.text: Kamu menelepon teman dan ingin tahu apakah orang tuanya ada di rumah.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Apakah orang tuamu di rumah?
question.explanation: **Your parents** = they, jadi kata kerjanya **are**. Dalam pertanyaan, **are** diletakkan sebelum subjek: **Are your parents** at home?

steps.title: Jawaban singkat
steps.text: Sekarang jawab pertanyaan dengan jawaban singkat.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Is your brother at work? — Yes, ___.
question.explanation: Jawaban singkat mengulang subjek dan be: **Yes, he is.** Untuk jawaban **Yes**, kita tidak memakai bentuk singkat 'he's', dan 'is he' adalah urutan pertanyaan.

steps.title: Ulasan cepat
steps.text: Balik kartu-kartu ini supaya bentuknya makin nempel.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk nanti, ya.

Jawaban singkat **Yes** memakai bentuk lengkap: **Yes, I am**, bukan 'Yes, I'm'.
